hooks.text: A giant star in our galaxy regularly chokes on its own soot.
What kind of star vanishes from the sky without even exploding?
There is a star that explodes in reverse to become invisible.

title: The Star That Chokes on Its Own Soot
description: R Coronae Borealis is a rare reverse nova that periodically vanishes as it smothers itself in clouds of carbon dust.

beats.text: A giant star in our galaxy regularly chokes on its own soot.
beats.visual: artist concept of a carbon star ejecting soot clouds and dust puffs
queries: Artist concept carbon star soot cloud

beats.text: Discovered in 1795, the supergiant R Coronae Borealis usually shines bright enough for the naked eye.
beats.visual: constellation map showing Corona Borealis and star locations

beats.text: But without warning, this "reverse nova" can plummet to nearly one-millionth of its normal brightness.
beats.visual: light curve graph showing R Coronae Borealis magnitude drops over time
queries: AAVSO light curve R Coronae Borealis
R Coronae Borealis light curve graph

beats.text: It doesn't explode outward like a typical star; instead, it suddenly vanishes from view for months.
beats.visual: artist concept of a carbon star with a dark dust shell
queries: NASA artist concept dust shell star

beats.text: Astronomers found the star is actually smothering itself in a massive cloud of carbon dust.
beats.visual: illustration of carbon dust puffs around a yellow supergiant

beats.text: Intense shockwaves force carbon gas to condense into thick, dark soot that blocks all visible light.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope observations of circumstellar dust around a variable star
queries: Hubble Space Telescope circumstellar dust nebula
Hubble Space Telescope imaging cosmic dust

beats.text: While it disappears from our eyes, infrared telescopes can see right through the cosmic smog.
beats.visual: comparison of optical versus infrared view of dust obscuration in deep space
queries: Barnard 68 visible and infrared comparison ESO
Hubble visible vs infrared dust penetration

beats.text: Radiation pressure eventually clears the exhaust, revealing why this giant star regularly chokes on its own soot.
beats.visual: artist concept of radiation pressure dispersing a stellar dust shell
queries: NASA artist concept dust shell star
White dwarf merger artist concept NASA

better_than_last: Improved retention by placing the most paradoxical term—'chokes on its own soot'—directly in the first five words of the hook as per evidence from ep008.
